objective: Repair the Bominal-regression critique by upgrading the sparse permitted modules area into a cohesive, Bominal-grade, locally interactive Service Catalog and Product Graph inside the Oyatie dashboard.

gap_analysis.source: user feedback that the current mockup is nowhere close to Bominal in visual, feature, or functionality and has regressed
findings_addressed: The old Modules area was a simple card grid and did not feel like a complete product surface.
It lacked Bominal-style operational density: KPIs, table scanning, owners, criticality, health, dependencies, and local action feedback.
It did not visibly connect Workflow, Messenger, Mail, Community, Cloud Ops, Finance, and Audit into one cohesive product graph.
Shell navigation and command palette did not treat Service Catalog as a first-class destination.

implemented: Replaced the simple permitted module card grid with a dense Service Catalog workbench inside the existing dashboard grid, not a separate page.
Added Bominal-style KPI strip for permitted modules, cloud dependencies, attention count, trust surfaces, and cross-suite routes.
Added search, group/state filters, visible-count/status feedback, table headers, module health dots, owner avatars, group chips, criticality chips, dependency chains, and per-module actions.
Added a Product Graph lineage rail showing Workflow fan-out to Messenger, Mail, Community, Cloud Ops, and Audit evidence.
Added local interactions for filtering/search, pinning, request-access staging, module open routing, graph route navigation, command palette Service Catalog entry, and activity feed mutation.
Extended SSR static markup and WASM-hydrated markup with the same Service Catalog structure so the surface remains visible before hydration and interactive after hydration.
Added CSS tokens/components for catalog KPIs, filters, table rows, owner/criticality chips, lineage rail, responsive collapse, and review-requested state.

observations: SSR output contains service-catalog, data-catalog-module, data-catalog-search, and data-catalog-graph-action markup

verification.command: Playwright smoke for Service Catalog hash route, search/filter, pin, request access, product graph route, command palette route, console/network health

visual_verdict.category_match: Bominal-style enterprise catalog / product graph adapted to Oyatie Control Center
visual_verdict.verdict: This slice removes a clear regression: the service catalog now reads as a real product surface with dense information architecture, local interactivity, and cross-suite lineage instead of a generic card grid. It is cohesive with the dashboard because it uses the same shell, activity center, side peek, command palette, and built-in Messenger/Mail/Community/Workflow routes.
improved_matches: Bominal-like table-first density, owner chips, criticality, health, KPI strip, and status feedback are now encoded in repo-native CSS/components.
The product graph explains how modules relate to Workflow, Messenger, Mail, Community, Cloud Ops, and Audit rather than presenting disconnected modules.
Search/filter/actions visibly mutate local state and feed notifications without pretending to persist backend changes.
SSR and selective hydration both preserve the feature: visible SSR markup plus local DOM interactivity after hydration.
remaining_differences: This is still a prototype shell: no real entitlement, catalog, route, workflow, audit, mail, messenger, or community backend is wired.
Bominal has full route-level apps; this slice improves one Oyatie dashboard surface and does not claim every remaining surface is fully complete.
Pixel diffs remain secondary debug evidence because this surface adapts Bominal design language to an Oyatie-specific service catalog rather than cloning one exact Bominal page.

non_claims: No real service catalog, entitlement system, workflow engine, mail/messenger/community transport, audit chain, cloud provider, or resource inventory is contacted.
No module access request, pin, graph route, or catalog status is persisted beyond local DOM state.
No claim is made that the long-running complete mockup goal is finished.
